metas.name: Arecaceae - Açai Palm (Belém Palm)
metas.note: The species is native to eastern Amazonia, especially in Brazil, mainly in swamps and floodplains.
metas.footer: Click -> Euterpe Oleracea for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Acrocomia Totai (Paraguay Palm)
metas.note: Found in eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, northern Argentina and southern Brazil (Matto Grosso do Sul). It is commonly mistaken to be a Macaw Palm (Acrocomia Aculeata). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences - Macaw Palm: More open and irregular, with leaves spreading in different directions. - "Paraguay Palm": Denser and more compact, sometimes looking neater and rounder.
metas.footer: Click -> Acrocomia Totai for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - African Oil Palm
metas.note: Elaeis Guineensis is an oil palm native to west and southwest Africa, specifically the area between Angola and The Gambia. The species is also now naturalised in many places, the most useful for Geoguessr are: Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Central America.
metas.footer: Click -> Elaeis Guineensis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - African Palmyra Palm
metas.note: It is widespread across much of tropical Africa from Senegal to Uganda and south to northern South Africa.
metas.footer: Click -> Borassus Aethiopum for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Alexandra Palm
metas.note: The native range of this species is north-east and central-east Queensland, from the Melville Range in Cape York Peninsula to south of Gladstone.
metas.footer: Click -> Archontophoenix Alexandrae for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Areca Palm
metas.note: Areca catechu is a species of palm native to the Philippines cultivated for areca nuts. It is widespread in cultivation and is considered naturalized in Malaysia, Indonesia, Taiwan, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, India (Assam and Kerala mostly), Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and more regions that are not in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Areca Catechu for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Asian Palmyra Palm (Cambodia Palm)
metas.note: Borassus Flabellifer is a fan palm native to South Asia especially Cambodia, Thailand, Bangladesh, India, Sri lanka, Indonesia (lesser nusa islands)
metas.footer: Click -> Borassus Flabellifer for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Babassu
metas.note: The Babassu is a palm native to the Amazon Rainforest region in South America. It is the predominant species in the Maranhão Babaçu forests of Brazil. It is also seen in amazonian states and rarely in Piauí and Tocantins. Not to be confused with other Attalea species like A. Phalerata and A.
metas.footer: Click -> Attalea Speciosa for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Cabbage Palmetto
metas.note: Sabal palmetto is native to the subtropical coastal regions of the American states of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, southeastern North Carolina, and extreme southern Texas. It is very similar to its relatives S. Yapa, S. Mexicana, S. Rosei
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Palmetto for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - California Fan Palm
metas.note: Washingtonia filifera is the only palm native to the Western United States and one of the country's largest native palms.
metas.footer: Click -> Washingtonia Filifera for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Canary Island Palm
metas.note: Phoenix Canariensis is native to the Canary Islands but is typically cultivated in wet-winter or Mediterranean climates and also in wet-summer or humid subtropical climates. It appears in many notable examples of landscaping, particularly in the American state of California.
metas.footer: Click -> Phoenix Canariensis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Caranday Palm
metas.note: Copernicia Alba is found in the Humid Chaco ecoregion in Bolivia, Paraguay, southern Brazil and northern Argentina. It can be hard to differenciate between C. Prunifera and C. Alba, one clue is that the C. Prunifera very often has visible gaps between the leaves, while the C. Alba has thicker, more densely packed leaves. The best way to identify them though is trying to tell by the landscape - if you're in northern Brazil or not.
metas.footer: Click -> Copernicia Alba for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Carnauba Palm (Ceará Palm)
metas.note: Copernicia Prunifera is a species of palm tree native to northeastern Brazil (mainly the states of Ceará, Piauí, Maranhão, Rio Grande do Norte and Bahia). It can be hard to differenciate between C. Prunifera and C. Alba, one clue is that the C. Prunifera very often has visible gaps between the leaves, while the C. Alba has thicker, more densely packed leaves. The best way to identify them though is trying to tell by the landscape - if you're in northern Brazil or not.
metas.footer: Click -> Copernicia Prunifera for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Chilean Wine Palm
metas.note: It is endemic to a small area of central Chile between southern Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Santiago, O'Higgins, and northern Maule regions. They are highly concentrated around Viña del Mar.
metas.footer: Click -> Jubaea Chilensis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Chinese Fan Palm
metas.note: It is native to southern Japan, Taiwan, the Ryukyu Islands, and other regions that are not in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Livistona Chinensis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Doum Palm
metas.note: It is a native to the Arabian Peninsula and also to the northern half and western part of Africa. If you see this palm in India, you will most likely be in the union territory of Daman and Diu (or close to it, in coastal Gujarat).
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Thebaica for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - East African Doum Palm
metas.note: This is a palm known for its unique branching, unlike most palms which are not branched. It is very abundant in Kenya, and also found in other countries not featured in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Compressa for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Florida Thatch Palm
metas.note: In the wild, this species almost always grows close to coastal areas. It is mostly found in southern Florida, Caribbean islands, and the eastern coast of the Yucatán peninsula in México. The key element to identify this palm between others found in similar areas, is the circular, fan shaped leaves.
metas.footer: Click -> Thrinax Radiata for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Ilala Palm
metas.note: The ilala palm is a species of palm tree native to the eastern Afrotropics. It occurs in Kwazulu-Natal (South Africa), the coastal flats of Madagascar and other countries that are not in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Coriacea for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Juçara Palm
metas.note: Closely related to the Açaí palm, they are really hard to distinguish apart from each other. However, the Açaí palm grows mostly in the northern flat regions of Brazil, while the Juçara grows in the mountainous south-east regions of Brazil anywhere from Espirito Santo down to Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Click -> Euterpe Edulis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Licuala Ramsayi
metas.note: The Queensland fan palm or Australian fan palm, is a species endemic to northeastern Queensland, Australia (Specially around Cairns).
metas.footer: Click -> Queensland Fan Palm for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Macaw Palm
metas.note: The species is found from southern Mexico and the Caribbean to Brazil, extending down to Paraguay and northern Argentina. It is commonly mistaken to be a "Paraguay Palm" (Acrocomia Totai). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences - Macaw Palm: More open and irregular, with leaves spreading in different directions. - "Paraguay Palm": Denser and more compact, sometimes looking neater and rounder.
metas.footer: Click -> Acrocomia Aculeata for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Makalani Palm
metas.note: This palm is similar to the Ilala Palm (H. Coriacea) the main difference is the shape of the stem, which regularly bulges out below the foliage. Its habitat, as seen in Geoguessr, is mostly in the northern half of Botswana and northern Limpopo.
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Petersiana for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Mediterranean Fan Palm
metas.note: Chamaerops humilis is one of only two palm species native to continental Europe, the other being Phoenix theophrasti. It is mainly found in southwestern Europe, in mediterranean coasts.
metas.footer: Click -> Chamaerops Humilis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Mexican Palmetto
metas.note: This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Mexicana for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Moriche Palm
metas.note: Mauritia flexuosa is found in the wild in streetview in: Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.
metas.footer: Click -> Mauritia Flexuosa for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Nibong Palm
metas.note: The Nibong palm is found in Southeast Asia: Southern Thailand and Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Philippines, always west of the Wallace Line. There seems to be a high concentration of them in Sumatra, Kalimantan, Peninsular Malaysia, and Java (according to Palmpedia.net).
metas.footer: Click -> Oncosperma Tigillarium for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Nikau Palm
metas.note: Rhopalostylis sapida, commonly known as nīkau, is a palm tree endemic to New Zealand, and the only palm native to mainland New Zealand.
metas.footer: Click -> Rhopalostylis Sapida for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Quindio Wax Palm
metas.note: The Quindío wax palm, is the tallest palm tree in the world and it is native to the humid montane forests of the Andes in Colombia and Peru.
metas.footer: Click -> Ceroxylon Quindiuense for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Sabal Rosei (Nayarit Palm)
metas.note: Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Rosei for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Sand Palm
metas.note: The sand palm is endemic to the north of the Northern Territory of Australia, from the Fitzmaurice River to Cape Arnhem and inland as far as Katherine.
metas.footer: Click -> Livistona Humilis for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Saw Palmetto
metas.note: It is endemic to the subtropical and tropical Southeastern United States as well as Mexico, most commonly along the south Atlantic and Gulf Coastal plains and sand hills. It grows in clumps or dense thickets in sandy coastal areas, and as undergrowth in pine woods or hardwood hammocks.
metas.footer: Click -> Serenoa Repens for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Thatch Palmetto
metas.note: This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Yapa for more information!

metas.name: Arecaceae - Trithrinax Campestris
metas.note: This palm shares the same habitat and common name (Caranday palm) as the Copernicia Alba. It is one of the most cold-hardy palms in the world, because it also grows in the mountains of Sierras de Córdoba and Sierras de San Luis.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Arecaceae - Yatay Palm
metas.note: Butia yatay is a Butia palm native to southern Brazil, Uruguay and northern Argentina.
metas.footer: Click -> Butia Yatay for more information!

metas.name: Asparagaceae - Tree Yucca
metas.note: It is native to central mexico, most commonly found in Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí although it can be seen anywhere from Nuevo León down to Puebla, in dry regions.
metas.footer: Click -> Yucca Filifera for more information!

metas.name: Aspleniaceae - Bird's-nest Fern
metas.note: It is native to temperate and tropical Asia, northern Australia, Pacific islands and other non-streetview regions (in Geoguessr, it is most commonly spotted in Southeast Asia). It can live as a terrestrial plant or an epyphite (A plant or plant-like organism that grows on the surface of another plant).
metas.footer: Click -> Asplenium Nidus for more information!

metas.name: Bromeliaceae - Orangeade Bromeliad
metas.note: It is found in the Atlantic forest biome in eastern Brazil. This plant grows from the State of Bahia south to Espírito Santo. The plant is most often seen being terrestrial, however it can be an epiphyte as well (A plant or plant-like organism that grows on the surface of another plant).
metas.footer: Click -> Aechmea Blanchetiana for more information!

metas.name: Bromeliaceae - Spanish Moss
metas.note: Spanish moss is an epiphytic (a plant that grows on another plant, especially one that is not parasitic) flowering plant that often grows upon large trees in tropical and subtropical climates. It is native to much of Mexico, Bermuda, Central America, South America, West Indies, and most noticeably, Southeastern United States. It must be noted that it is extremely similar to Beard Moss which is from a different family.
metas.footer: Click -> Tillandsia Usneoides for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Andes Organ Pipe
metas.note: Cereus hildmannianus is a species of cactus from southern South America. Its distribution is uncertain but probably includes Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina.
metas.footer: Click -> Cereus Hildmannianus for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Argentine Saguaro
metas.note: It is native to several provinces including Jujuy, Tucumán, La Rioja, San Juan, Catamarca and Salta provinces in northwestern Argentina, and is the eponymous cactus of Los Cardones National Park in Salta Province.
metas.footer: Click -> Trichocereus Terscheckii for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Armatocereus Matucanensis
metas.note: Armatocereus matucanensis is a species of Armatocereus from Ecuador and Peru. There's many species of Armatocereus, I just picked the one that was easier to find and identify. They generally look very similar and are found in the same places so it's not that important.
metas.footer: Click -> Armatocereus Matucanensis for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Blue Myrtle
metas.note: Myrtillocactus Geometrizans is a species of cactus in the genus Myrtillocactus, native to central and northern Mexico. It is especially abundant in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo, and much more rarely Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Click -> Myrtillocactus Geometrizans for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Cactus Acido
metas.note: Eulychnia acida, commonly known as cactus ácido or copao, is a cactus species endemic to Chile, where it is primarily distributed in the semi-arid regions of the country. Its range includes: Atacama Region, Coquimbo Region,and Valparaíso Region.
metas.footer: Click -> Eulychnia Acida for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Candelabro
metas.note: Pachycereus weberi is widespread in the Mexican states of Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at altitudes of 600 to 1,500 m.
metas.footer: Click -> Pachycereus Weberi for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Caxacubri
metas.note: The distribution area of Xiquexique Tuberculatus extends from the northwest to the northeast of the Brazilian state of Bahia and extends into the state of Pernambuco. It can easily be confused with its brother the Xiquexique Gounellei - X. Tuberculatus has thinner shoots with less ribs, and shorter spines.
metas.footer: Click -> Xiquexique Tuberculatus for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Chiotilla
metas.note: The species originates from Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, southern Puebla). It will almost always place you somewhere in Oaxaca, usually central in the state.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Cactaceae - Column Cactus
metas.note: There is two main subspecies of this cactus, they are hard to tell apart through streetview imagery so I'll treat them as the same cactus. It's found in south Ecuador, Perú, and Bolivia.
metas.footer: Click -> Trichocereus Macrogonus for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Dagger Cactus
metas.note: This species is mostly found in the dry regions of Colombia (mostly in Guajira, Tatacoa desert) and the ABC islands of the Dutch Caribbean (only Curaçao is in geoguessr).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Cactaceae - Giant Cardon
metas.note: Pachycereus pringlei is a species of large cactus native to northwestern Mexico, in the states of Baja California, Baja California Sur, and Sonora.
metas.footer: Click -> Pachycereus Pringlei for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Jumping Cholla
metas.note: Cylindropuntia fulgida is a cholla cactus native to Sonora and the Southwestern United States.
metas.footer: Click -> Cylindropuntia Fulgida for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Mandacaru
metas.note: Cereus jamacaru, known as mandacaru or cardeiro is a cactus native to central and eastern Brazil.
metas.footer: Click -> Cereus Jamacaru for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Neoraimondia Arequipensis
metas.note: N. arequipensis is endemic to Peru, where it is found in Arequipa, Ayacucho, Cajamarca, Huancavelica, Lima, Lambayique, Piura and sometimes other regions. It commonly grows in rocky coastal habitats, desert scrub and inter-Andean valleys.
metas.footer: Click -> Neoraimondia Arequipensis for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Opuntia Quimilo
metas.note: Opuntia quimilo is a species of Prickly Pear belonging to the Cactaceae family. It is found in north-central Argentina and is widespread in Bolivia. The Opuntia (Prickly Pears) have been spread out through the world and they all look very similar, but within each country that has them, it is often possible to regionguess when you see them.
metas.footer: Click -> Opuntia Quimilo for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Organ Pipe
metas.note: This species is found mostly in Mexico, mainly in Sonora and southern Baja California and Northern Sinaloa. It is also found in the Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument in southern Arizona and ocasionally elsewhere in southern Arizona.
metas.footer: Click -> Stenocereus Thurberi for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Pilosocereus Pachycladus
metas.note: Similar story to the Armatocereus in Perú. This cactus has many species but they are all found in north-eastern Brazil and generally look very similar. I just chose to include the P. Pachycladus in the map.
metas.footer: Click -> Pilosocereus Pachycladus for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Pitaya De Queretaro
metas.note: Stenocereus queretaroensis is a species of cactus from Mexico, mostly in the states of Querétaro, Guanajuato and Jalisco. It is cultivated for its fruit.
metas.footer: Click -> Stenocereus Queretaroensis for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Pitayo De Aguas
metas.note: This cactus is really rare to see in Streetview since the area where it is commonly found lacks coverage, but if you see it, you're most likely be on the 37D in Michoacán.
metas.footer: Click -> Stenocereus Fricii for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Quisco
metas.note: Echinopsis Chiloensis occur along the coast and in the coastal cordillera of Chile (North-Central Valley of Chile) in the regions of Maule, O'Higgins, Metropolitana, Valparaíso and Coquimbo, from Talca to Valle del Elqui.
metas.footer: Click -> Trichocereus Chiloensis for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Saguaro
metas.note: The Saguaro is endemic to the Sonoran Desert and is found primarily in western Sonora in Mexico, and in western Arizona in the US. Elevation is a limiting factor to its environment, as the saguaro is sensitive to extended frost or cold temperatures.
metas.footer: Click -> Carnegiea Gigantea for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Toothpick Cactus
metas.note: Stetsonia coryne is distributed in high-altitude arid regions, such as the deserts and dry forest (Gran Chaco) of northwestern Argentina, as well as in Bolivia, Paraguay, and the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso do Sul.
metas.footer: Click -> Stetsonia Coryne for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Tree Cholla
metas.note: Cylindropuntia imbricata is a cactus found in the Southwestern United States and northern Mexico, including some cooler regions in comparison to many other cacti. It occurs primarily in the arid regions of the Southwestern United States in the states of Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado, and Nevada.
metas.footer: Click -> Cylindropuntia Imbricata for more information!

metas.name: Cactaceae - Xique-Xique
metas.note: Xiquexique Gounellei is widespread in northeastern Brazil in the Caatinga vegetation. It can easily be confused with its brother the Xiquexique Tuberculatus - X. Gounellei has thicker shoots with more ribs and longer spines.
metas.footer: Click -> Xiquexique Gounellei for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Bunya Pine
metas.note: The Bunya pine's natural range is southeast Queensland. There are many planted specimens throughout the world due to its very aesthetic appearance.
metas.footer: Click -> Araucaria Bidwillii for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Dahurian Larch
metas.note: The Dahurian Larch is a species of larch native to eastern Siberia and adjacent northeastern Mongolia, South Korea, and other countries not featured in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Larix gmelinii for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Douglas Fir
metas.note: The Douglas fir is native to western North America and despite its common names, it is not a true fir, spruce, or pine. It's a "false hemlock".
metas.footer: Click -> Pseudotsuga Menziesii for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Jack Pine
metas.note: Jack pines are found in Canada mostly anywhere east of the Rockies, but in US they can actually be really good to regionguess since they mostly grow from Minnesota to Maine, almost always on sandy and rocky soil. Their scraggly, irregular shape is similar to the Pitch pine. However their distribution is very similar to the Red pine (P. Resinosa).
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Banksiana for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Khasi Pine
metas.note: The Khasi Pine's range extends from Meghalaya India to northern Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and most noticeably in the Luzon tropical pine forests of the Philippines where it is also known as the Benguet Pine. (I excluded non-geoguessr countries from the list).
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Kesiya for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Loblolly Pine
metas.note: Pinus taeda, commonly known as Loblolly pine, is one of several pines native to the Southeastern United States. It can be easily mistaken with the Red pine (P. Resinosa) since they both have clumps of needles at the end of the branch, however, the clumps from the Loblolly appear bigger in size and less "rounded" compared to the Red pine. The clumps of the Red pine when seen from afar look dark green or even black.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Taeda for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Monkey Puzzle
metas.note: The closest relative to the Paraná Pine, this tree's native habitat is the lower slopes of the Chilean and Argentine south-central Andes.
metas.footer: Click -> Araucaria Araucana for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Parana Pine
metas.note: Besides southern Brazil, it is also found in high-altitude areas of southern Minas Gerais, in central Rio de Janeiro and in the east and south of São Paulo, but more typically in the states of Paraná, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Click -> Araucaria Angustifolia for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Pitch Pine
metas.note: Pitch pine is found mainly in the southern areas of the northeastern United States, from coastal Maine and Ohio to Kentucky and northern Georgia.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Rigida for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Red Pine
metas.note: Pinus resinosa, known as red pine (also Norway pine in Minnesota), is a pine native to Eastern North America, with a similar distribution to the Jack pines (P. Banksiana). It can be easily mistaken with the Loblolly pine (P. Taeda) since they both have clumps of needles at the end of the branch, however, the clumps from the Red pine appear "rounded" and smaller in size compared to those from the Loblolly pine. The clumps of the Red pine when seen from afar look dark green or even black.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Resinosa for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Scots Pine
metas.note: The Scots Pine / Baltic pine / European Red Pine is a species of tree in the pine family Pinaceae that is native to Eurasia. The best use for it in Geoguessr is to clear a possible confusion between North America and Europe / Russia.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Sylvestris for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Stone Pine
metas.note: The tree is native to the Mediterranean region, occurring in Southern Europe and the Levant. The species was introduced into North Africa millennia ago, and is also naturalized in the Canary Islands, South Africa and New South Wales.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Pinea for more information!

metas.name: Conifers - Sumatran Pine
metas.note: The Sumatran pine, is a pine native to the Malesia region of southeast Asia, and the only one that occurs naturally south of the equator. It is found mainly in North Sumatra and Java (rarely in Sulawesi) and also in Philippines in Mindoro and Palawan.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Merkusii for more information!

metas.name: Euphorbiaceae - Common Tree Euphorbia
metas.note: The plant occurs in Botswana, South Africa (in the north and east of the country), Rwanda, Uganda, Kenya, Eswatini and other african countries that do not have official streetview coverage. It is often confused to be a cactus but it actually belongs to a completely different family called Euphorbiaceae.
metas.footer: Click -> Euphorbia Ingens for more information!

metas.name: Fabaceae - Ghaf
metas.note: The Ghaf is native to arid portions of Western Asia and the Indian Subcontinent, but mostly seen through streetview in India, Oman, and most noticeably the United Arab Emirates.
metas.footer: Click -> Prosopis Cineraria for more information!

metas.name: Fabaceae - Honey Mesquite
metas.note: The plant is primarily native to the Southwestern United States and Northern Mexico.
metas.footer: Click -> Neltuma Glandulosa for more information!

metas.name: Fabaceae - Umbrella Thorn Acacia
metas.note: The Umbrella Thorn Acacia aka Acacia Tortilis is a large canopied tree native to most of Africa and Middle East. In streetview it is mostly seen in the countries of Kenya, Botswana, South Africa, Israel, Jordan, UAE and Oman.
metas.footer: Click -> Vachellia Tortilis for more information!

metas.name: Fouquieriaceae - Ocotillo
metas.note: The Ocotillo is a plant indigenous to Southwestern United States (southern California, southern Nevada, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas), and northern Mexico (as far south as Hidalgo and Guerrero).
metas.footer: Click -> Fouquieria Splendens for more information!

metas.name: Gunneraceae - Chilean Rhubarb (Chile Cabbage)
metas.note: Chilean rhubarb, or nalca, is a flowering plant species native to southern Chile and neighboring zones in Argentina. In some countries, such as New Zealand, the United Kingdom and Ireland, it has spread from gardens and is becoming an introduced species of concern.
metas.footer: Click -> Gunnera Tinctoria for more information!

metas.name: Malvaceae - African Baobab
metas.note: In streetview, these trees will mostly be found in: Senegal, Nigeria (Northeast), Kenya (Eastern half) and South Africa (Northern Limpopo).
metas.footer: Click -> Adansonia Digitata for more information!

metas.name: Malvaceae - Balsa Tree
metas.note: Valued across the world for its strong but light wood, the balsa tree is native to the rainforests of South America. Just like the trumpet bush (Cecropia), learning how to identify this plant by its leaves can help you guarantee that you are in South America.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Malvaceae - Boab Tree
metas.note: The Boab is endemic to the northern regions of Western Australia and the Northern Territory of Australia.
metas.footer: Click -> Adansonia Gregorii for more information!

metas.name: Malvaceae - Ceibo
metas.note: These trees appear in the drought deciduous forests ("bosque seco") in northern Peru and southern Ecuador.
metas.footer: Click -> Ceiba Trischistandra for more information!

metas.name: Malvaceae - Giant Baobab
metas.note: This baobab occurs in south-western Madagascar. It used to inhabit dry, deciduous forest but today it is mainly found in open, agricultural land or degraded scrubland.
metas.footer: Click -> Adansonia Grandidieri for more information!

metas.name: Polypodiaceae - Rock-ginger Fern
metas.note: (Also known as Drynaria Coronans) It is a species of tropical fern widely distributed throughout Southeast Asia, from Nepal to Peninsular Malaysia. In streetview seems to be very commonly spotted in Taiwan, often attached to Areca Palm trunks.
metas.footer: Click -> Aglaomorpha Coronans for more information!

metas.name: Urticaceae - Trumpet Bush
metas.note: Its geographic distribution extends along the Pacific and Atlantic Mexican coasts and in Central and South American forests. It is native to the Neotropics (tropical terrestrial ecoregions of the Americas and the entire South American temperate zone), which means it's a great clue to eliminate any Americas - Southeast Asia tossups.
metas.footer: Click -> Cecropia for more information!
